title: trataka
hook: binding the mind to one place: Patanjali's whole definition of concentration fits in a breath
carry: the mind tied to one place

segments.voice: Yesterday, trataka in two halves: the flame in front of the eyes, then the image held behind them.

Binding the mind to one place. That's Patanjali's whole definition of concentration, and it fits in a single breath. Just a mind, a place, and something tying the one to the other. A calf on a rope around a post can wander, but only so far, and it keeps circling back to the post. Trataka has spent three days putting a flame, a mark, an after-image in front of the mind. Today, the name the Yoga Sutras give to what's being trained.
screen: `BINDING THE MIND TO ONE PLACE.` → `A MIND, A PLACE, A TIE.` → `WHAT IS TRATAKA TRAINING?`

segments.voice: The third chapter of the Yoga Sutras opens with dharana. In paraphrase: dharana is the binding of the mind to a place. The sutra's word for binding is bandha, tying something down. The place can be a point in the body, Vyasa's commentary says, like the navel or the tip of the nose, or an outer object. The next sutra names what grows out of it: dhyana, meditation, when the mind's attention flows toward that place without a break. So dharana is the tying, and dhyana is when the rope goes slack because the calf has stopped pulling. Trataka is dharana you can see. The place is right there on the table. When the eyes drift, the drift is visible, and so is the coming back. And what should the place be? Patanjali is generous here. In the first chapter, after offering several supports for steadying the mind, he adds one more, in paraphrase: or by meditating on whatever one finds agreeable. The flame isn't required. A mark on the wall, a picture of a deity, a flower. What matters is the tie. Now look back at this week. The sankalpa, the short resolve. The senses gathered in, like rays into the setting sun. The watcher, awake in those who sleep. Then trataka opened the eyes: the Hatha Yoga Pradipika's still gaze at a small mark, the Gita's lamp in a windless place, the eyes turned around. And today, the name for all of it: the mind, tied to one place.
screen: `DHARANA: THE MIND TIED TO A PLACE.` · `DHYANA: ATTENTION FLOWING THERE UNBROKEN.` · `WHATEVER ONE FINDS AGREEABLE.` · `THIS WEEK: RESOLVE, GATHERING, GAZE.` · then, large: `TRATAKA IS DHARANA YOU CAN SEE.`

segments.voice: Choose your place, a candle flame safely lit, a mark on the wall, a flower or a picture that matters to you, and set it at eye level. Rest the eyes on it and picture a soft rope running from your attention to that point; when the mind wanders, let it reach the end of the rope, feel the tug, and walk back. If the eyes tire, close them and keep the point in mind.
Trataka. A still gaze at one small point. Today, dharana you can see: the mind tied to one place, and walking back each time it pulls away.
Your line: the mind tied to one place. A week of resolve, gathering and gaze. That's day one thousand twenty-nine.

howItsDone: In yoga traditions that follow Patanjali, trataka is taught as a training in dharana, holding attention on a single chosen object; practitioners pick a flame, a mark, a sacred image or a flower.
